# Nutrient Sign

> Full-stack document signing app built with Next.js and the Nutrient Web SDK

## What This Is

A sample signing application: upload PDFs, place signature fields, send to recipients via email, collect electronic signatures, and apply digital signatures via the Nutrient DWS API. Published as a reference implementation and starter template — no claims are made about its legal validity, regulatory compliance, or security.

## Tech Stack

- Next.js 16 (App Router, TypeScript, Turbopack)
- Nutrient Web SDK (@nutrient-sdk/viewer) for PDF viewing and annotation
- Nutrient DWS API for server-side digital signatures
- PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM
- Auth.js (Google + Microsoft OAuth)
- AWS S3 for document storage
- Resend or SendGrid for email
- Tailwind CSS 4, Radix UI, React Zero UI
- Terraform for infrastructure

## Architecture

### Signing Flow

1. Owner uploads PDF → S3
2. Owner places signature/initials/date fields per recipient
3. System emails each recipient a unique `/sign/[token]` link
4. Recipient signs electronically (draw, type, or image)
5. After all sign: DWS Build API appends blank page → DWS Sign API applies CAdES B-LT signature → signed PDF uploaded to S3

### Key Patterns

- Document proxy (`/api/documents/proxy`) handles both session auth and token auth
- Nutrient viewer loaded from CDN, wrapped in `lib/nutrient-viewer.ts`
- Digital signatures applied server-side in `lib/digital-signing.ts`
- System templates seeded on startup via `instrumentation.ts`
- Soft delete with trash/restore pattern

## Important Files

- `lib/digital-signing.ts` — DWS API integration (build + sign)
- `lib/nutrient-viewer.ts` — PDF viewer SDK wrapper (load, unload, dark mode)
- `lib/email-service.ts` — Email sending (Resend/SendGrid)
- `lib/auth/auth-js.ts` — Auth.js config with Microsoft photo handling
- `lib/s3.ts` — S3 client configuration
- `app/api/documents/proxy/route.ts` — S3 document proxy with dual auth
- `app/api/sign/submit/route.ts` — Signature submission endpoint
- `app/sign/[token]/page.tsx` — Public signing page
- `app/(protected)/send/components/steps/FieldPlacement.tsx` — Field placement UI
- `database/drizzle/document-signing-schema.ts` — Full database schema
- `database/drizzle/auth-schema.ts` — Auth tables

## API Routes

- `GET/POST /api/documents` — List/create documents
- `GET /api/documents/proxy` — Stream PDF from S3 (session or token auth)
- `POST /api/documents/[id]/send` — Send document to recipients
- `POST /api/sign/submit` — Submit a signature
- `POST /api/sign/decline` — Decline to sign
- `POST /api/sign/verify-token` — Validate signing token
- `POST /api/upload` — Upload document to S3
- `GET/POST /api/templates` — Template management

## Database Tables

- `documents` — PDF metadata, status (DRAFT→PENDING→COMPLETED), file paths
- `document_templates` — Reusable templates (system + user-created)
- `document_participants` — Recipients with access levels (VIEWER/SIGNER/CC)
- `signature_requests` — Per-recipient signing status and access tokens
- `document_annotations` — PDF annotations (JSONB)
- `document_audit_log` — Full audit trail with IP/user agent
- `document_notifications` — Email delivery tracking

## Environment Variables

See `.env.sample` for the complete list. Key groups: AUTH_*, DATABASE_URL, RESEND_KEY, AWS_*, NEXT_PUBLIC_NUTRIENT_*.
